q-124392.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229367/assets/e597e317f32a2a9a3757ce583a2b053f4cba1da1a2119c572671e7edc96c61e4.png)

The point $P(\frac{6}{7},\frac{\sqrt{13}}{7})$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta ?$
q-124392.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229367/assets/fb0da765a857607ce0c8f13690efaa2f0d504ccaa51899a23044ee4ed17f0aa5.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{6}{7}$ and $y=\frac{\sqrt{13}}{7}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{6}{7},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{7}.
$$

Knowing that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },$ we can calculate $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta :$

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{13}}{7})}{(\frac{6}{7})}=\frac{\sqrt{13}}{6}.
$$

EXPLANATION

Any point (x,y) on the unit circle is related to the central angle θ as follows:

x=cos⁡θ,y=sin⁡θ

cos⁡θ=67,sin⁡θ=137.

Knowing that tan⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θ, we can calculate tan⁡θ: tan⁡θ=(137)(67)=136.
